cards.headline: Tensix: 108 independent compute cores per chip
cards.body: Each TT chip packs 108 Tensix cores in a 12×9 grid. Every core has 1.5 MB local SRAM and a matrix/vector unit that runs independently — no shared register file, no cache coherence overhead. This is why TT hardware scales linearly with chip count.

cards.headline: 100 Gb/s on-package Ethernet
cards.body: TT chips connect via Ethernet fabric at 100 Gb/s. An allreduce across 4 chips takes ~1 µs — far less than one transformer layer's compute time. No proprietary interconnect license required.

cards.headline: TT Metal: zero Python overhead at inference
cards.body: TT Metal compiles ops into a static kernel-dispatch sequence. At inference time there is zero Python GIL overhead — the compiled trace replays RISC-V dispatches directly. This is why the trace capture stage during loading is worth the wait.

cards.headline: Trace capture = JIT compilation
cards.body: The trace_capture stage compiles separate graphs for 10 context lengths (128 → 65408 tokens). After capture, every inference replays a pre-built trace — no re-compilation per request. The first request after loading is just as fast as the thousandth.

cards.headline: Paged KV attention keeps batches full
cards.body: KV cache is divided into 16-token blocks, eliminating fragmentation. New requests join mid-generation without stalling existing decodes — hardware utilization stays high across concurrent users.

cards.headline: Wormhole vs Blackhole generations
cards.body: Wormhole (N150/N300/T3K) shipped 2022. Blackhole (P100/P150/P300) shipped 2024 with larger per-core SRAM, faster interconnect, and better int8 throughput. Both run the same TT Metal stack.

cards.headline: Column-parallel weight sharding
cards.body: Attention matrices are sharded column-wise across chips: each holds Q_proj of shape [hidden × (hidden÷N)]. Activations flow over Ethernet fabric — not through host DRAM — reducing round-trip latency ~100×.

cards.headline: GQA reduces KV bandwidth 8×
cards.body: Grouped-Query Attention shares KV heads across query groups. Llama-3 uses 8 KV heads for 64 query heads — 8× smaller KV cache and matching reduction in decode memory bandwidth. This is why Llama models can sustain high batch sizes.

cards.headline: HF cache: no re-download after first pull
cards.body: Model weights cached in ~/.cache/huggingface are mounted read-only into the Docker container. Weights stream disk→chip at ~7 GB/s via PCIe — no internet required after the first download.

cards.headline: tt-smi: device management in one command
cards.body: 'tt-smi -s' gives a JSON snapshot of temperature, utilization, and firmware. 'tt-smi -r' soft-resets all TT devices — required when switching between model families that use incompatible memory layouts.

cards.headline: Mixture of Experts: only 13B active per token
cards.body: Mixtral 8×7B has 45B total parameters but only 13B are active per token. The MoE router selects 2 of 8 expert FFN blocks per token — same quality as a dense 13B model at a fraction of the compute.

cards.headline: Whisper was trained on 680,000 hours of audio
cards.body: OpenAI's Whisper is a sequence-to-sequence transformer trained on 680K hours of multilingual audio. The large-v3 variant supports 99 languages and achieves near-human accuracy on clean speech.

cards.headline: Vision transformers: no convolutions needed
cards.body: ViT splits an image into 16×16 patches and treats them as tokens — the same self-attention mechanism as a language model, applied to image patches. Google's original ViT-Base uses 86M parameters.

cards.headline: FLUX uses flow matching, not diffusion
cards.body: FLUX.1 uses flow matching instead of the traditional DDPM diffusion process. This allows high-quality generation in as few as 4 steps (schnell variant) vs. 20–50 steps for older diffusion models.

cards.headline: Embeddings turn text into searchable geometry
cards.body: BGE and Qwen3-Embedding models convert text into vectors where semantic similarity = cosine similarity. Two sentences about the same topic land close together in this space — even if they share no words.

cards.headline: State-space models: no attention required
cards.body: Mamba uses a selective state-space model instead of attention. Inference scales linearly with sequence length (not quadratically), making it fast for very long contexts with a constant-size state.
